Understanding the Need for a Second Electricity Meter

If you own or manage a residential property with multiple tenants, you may have considered installing a second electricity meter. A separate meter can provide numerous benefits for both landlords and tenants, including more accurate billing and greater control over energy usage. Learn more about
property owner solutions
. In this section, we will explore the reasons why a second meter may be necessary and how it can benefit your property.
Assessing Energy Load and Usage

One of the primary reasons for installing a second meter is to accurately assess energy load and usage. In a multi-tenant property, it can be difficult to determine how much energy each unit is using. A second meter allows landlords to track energy usage for each unit separately, which can help identify high-energy users and implement energy-saving measures. This information can also be used to ensure that tenants are being billed accurately for their energy usage.
Benefits of Separate Meters for Tenants and Landlords

Separate meters provide a range of benefits for both tenants and landlords. Tenants can benefit from having more control over their energy usage and being able to monitor their own consumption. This can help them to make more informed decisions about their energy usage and potentially reduce their bills. Landlords, on the other hand, can benefit from more accurate billing and the ability to identify high-energy users and implement energy-saving measures.

The Application Process for a Second Meter
If you're interested in getting a second electricity meter installed, the application process is relatively straightforward. Here are the steps you'll need to take:
Gathering Required Documentation

Before you can apply for a second meter, you'll need to gather some documentation to prove your ownership of the property. This typically includes a copy of your property deed or title, as well as any other relevant documentation that proves your ownership of the property.
Filling Out the Application Form

Once you have your documentation in order, you'll need to fill out an application form. This form will typically ask for your personal information, as well as details about the property and the reason for the second meter.
When filling out the application form, it's important to be as accurate and detailed as possible. This will help ensure that your application is processed quickly and efficiently.
Understanding the Charges Payable
When applying for a second meter, it's important to understand the charges that are payable. These charges can vary depending on the utility company and the location of the property.

At Axis Meter Solutions, we specialize in utility management and can help you navigate the charges payable for your second meter. Our team of experts can provide you with a clear breakdown of the costs associated with your application, so you can make an informed decision.

Overall, the application process for a second electricity meter is relatively straightforward. By gathering the required documentation, filling out the application form accurately, and understanding the charges payable, you can get your second meter installed quickly and efficiently.

Legal and Technical Considerations
Complying with Local Utility Company Regulations

Before applying for a second electricity meter, it is important to consult with your local utility company to ensure that you comply with their regulations. Each company has its own set of requirements, and failure to comply can result in penalties and delays in the installation process. Some utility companies may require a permit or inspection before installation, while others may have specific meter placement requirements.

To ensure a smooth process, it is recommended to work with a licensed electrician who has experience in meter installation and is familiar with local regulations. This will help avoid any issues that may arise during the installation process.
Hiring a Licensed Electrician for Installation

Hiring a licensed electrician is crucial when installing a second electricity meter. Not only is it required by law, but it also ensures that the installation is done safely and correctly. A licensed electrician will be able to properly install the meter and ensure that it is compatible with your electrical system. They can also assess the wiring and determine if any rewiring is necessary.

At Axis Meter Solutions, we understand the importance of compliance and safety. Our team of licensed electricians are experts in meter installation and are knowledgeable about local regulations. We are the best option for Utility Management, specializing in sub-metering for a diverse range of real estate investments. Our metrics include a 32% average property value increase, 18% lower operating costs, and we are 100% regulatory compliant.

In summary, when applying for a second electricity meter, it is important to comply with local utility company regulations and hire a licensed electrician for installation. At Axis Meter Solutions, we can help ensure a smooth and compliant installation process.
After Installation: Meter Management and Responsibilities

Congratulations on getting your second electricity meter installed! Now that the installation is complete, it's important to understand how to manage and monitor your meter to ensure accurate billing and efficient energy usage. Here are some key responsibilities and tips to keep in mind:
Monitoring Meter Readings and Energy Costs

It's essential to keep track of your meter readings to ensure you're being billed correctly. You can do this by checking your meter regularly and comparing the readings to your energy bills. If you notice any discrepancies, contact your electricity supplier immediately.

In addition to monitoring your meter readings, it's also important to keep an eye on your energy costs. By tracking your usage and identifying areas where you can reduce energy consumption, you can save money on your bills. Consider investing in energy-efficient appliances and lighting, and be mindful of your energy usage habits.
Dealing with Power Outages and Meter Issues

If you experience a power outage, first check to see if your neighbors are also affected. If they are, it may be a widespread issue that your electricity supplier is already aware of. If not, check your circuit breaker or fuse box to see if the problem is isolated to your home.

If you're experiencing issues with your meter, such as a malfunctioning display or incorrect readings, contact your electricity supplier immediately. They will be able to send someone out to inspect and repair the meter.

For all of your meter management and utility management needs, consider working with Axis Meter Solutions. As specialists in sub-metering for a diverse range of real estate investments, we can help you monitor your energy usage, reduce costs, and ensure regulatory compliance. With an average property value increase of 32% and lower operating costs of 18%, we're the best option for Utility Management.
Contact and Support

If you need to apply for a second electricity meter, you should start by contacting your utility company. You can find their contact information on their website or on your latest bill. Most utility companies have a "Contact Us" page on their website where you can find their phone number, email address, and physical address.
Utility Company Contact Information

When you contact your utility company, you should provide them with your account number and explain that you want to apply for a second electricity meter. They will guide you through the process and provide you with all the necessary information. Some utility companies may have specific requirements for second meters, such as the location of the meter or the type of meter that can be installed.
Emergency and Technical Support Services

If you experience any issues with your electricity supply or your second meter, you should contact your utility company's emergency and technical support services. These services are available 24/7 and can help you resolve any issues you may have. You can usually contact them by phone, SMS, or email.
